title: ‘Babylon on the Potomac’: Pete Hegseth’s Radical DC Church Attracts Government Elites
author: Tess Owen
text:
On a Sunday morning in April, minutes from the US Capitol and down a stretch of Washington, DC’s Pennsylvania Avenue, a wall of black SUVs lined up alongside yellow police tape. Men in military gear held long guns and guarded the entrance to a mirrored window and door.This is Christ Church DC, a place of worship that appeared on Capitol Hill a year ago.That Sunday, high-ranking government officials, including Homeland Security's intelligence chief, America’s top international health diplomat, and the government’s international finance chief, had gathered to hear a sermon. “It gives a whole new meaning to worshipping in the presence of your enemies,” quipped the pastor, referencing the church’s location. “We’ve asked the government to fix us, and we’re more enslaved than ever.”Featured VideoThe Best Political Metaphor of the Year? How About a $15m Stagnant PoolChrist Church DC arrived after Pete Hegseth, who regularly attends worship with his family, was confirmed as US secretary of defense.The church is part of Pastor Doug Wilson’s network, known as the CREC—the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches—which is headquartered in Moscow, Idaho. Wilson’s long-held goal is to turn America into a theocracy, where all its institutions are molded in accordance with biblical law, executions are made public, non-Christians are barred from holding office, and women submit to their husbands instead of voting.WIRED has identified around a dozen government officials who have attended services at Christ Church DC at least once since it opened a year ago. Other officials who have attended include a top-ranking Pentagon adviser, a former senior Marine Corps pilot who now oversees personnel affairs in the Navy, and a federal immigration judge with a history of attracting complaints of volatile outbursts toward colleagues.Wilson calls DC “Babylon on the Potomac,” a biblical moniker he uses to evoke a corrupt place populated by ungodly people. The church has occupied three different locations since it was established, and Wilson has been raising funds to buy a permanent home for it. “We are here for the long haul,” he wrote in a blog post earlier this year. “We believe that it is our responsibility to begin pursuing opportunities to purchase a building near Capitol Hill.” He has also advised on his podcast to not “go to DC and go native” and “[climb] the greasy pole of ambition.” Rather, he said DC “needs an infusion of God-fearing humans.”Wilson, who initially agreed to an interview with WIRED and then abruptly canceled with little explanation, hasn’t shied away in past media engagements from touting his newfound clout in government circles. “This is the first time we’ve had connections with as many people in national government as we do now,” Wilson told the Associated Press in 2025, shortly after he came to DC to speak at the opening of his new church.

After he was narrowly confirmed as secretary of defense last year, Hegseth introduced a regular monthly Pentagon prayer service and brought out his pastor from Tennessee, Brooks Potteiger, to lead the inaugural session. In July, Potteiger officially became the pastor of Christ Church DC.“I believe this is significant,” Potteiger said on a podcast with Wilson and other church elders before his move to DC. “It energizes me … to see these young families, and especially the young Christian men, who are hungry for a soaring biblical view of the lordship of Christ over all things.” (Christ Church DC did not respond to WIRED’s request for an interview with Potteiger.)As secretary, Hegseth has invoked scripture when talking about the war in Iran, established an office of religious affairs at the Pentagon, and used his position to claim that America is a fundamentally Christian nation. "Our department is, you might say, putting on the full armor of God, because while we wage physical war, we all know the real battle is spiritual," Hegseth said in a speech in late September. "Live your calling. Stand firm. Preach truth. Minister to the flock." He has invited Wilson to speak at Pentagon prayer sessions twice this year. In Wilson’s most recent address to the military, just last week, he told his audience why they are right to want America to become a theocracy and why they are right to want to impose a Christian conservative social order.Most PopularDealsCan’t Wait for Black Friday? He’s been seeding his influence through his network of around 160 churches and hundreds of CREC-accredited schools and colleges across the US and internationally, laying the groundwork to take his blueprint for a Christian nationalist society well beyond Idaho. Wilson has made it explicitly clear that he is building toward a new political and social order in America—one that places the church at its center and is ruled by Christian men.Through various affiliated media outlets, Wilson has said “women need to be pastored, and they need to be pastored by men,” and as recently as 2024 he advocated for the repeal of the 19th Amendment, which gave women the right to vote. This belief system goes back decades: In 1996 he coauthored a booklet describing slavery as a “relationship based upon mutual affection and confidence.” He has said that he doesn’t believe that “a Muslim should be able to hold political office” and called immigration a “deliberately fomented war on the American heritage and unremitting hostility to the culture.”Wilson’s reach into the US government now extends beyond Hegseth. Christ Church DC’s new worshipers include Justin Overbaugh, deputy undersecretary of war for intelligence and security at the Defense department; Nate Halverson, chief of staff to the assistant secretary of the Navy for manpower and reserve affairs; C. Scott “Sonny” Duncan, senior counselor to the secretary of the Navy; Stuart Scheller, senior adviser to the US undersecretary of war for personnel and readiness; and Ryan Higgins, senior adviser for religious issues at the Pentagon and one of Hegseth’s key aides.Overbaugh, a former US Army officer who was working in risk management in Florida until Hegseth nominated him, now deals with highly sensitive military intelligence and counterintelligence. Overbaugh is an attendee of Christ Church DC and is slated to give a seminar in Tampa, Florida, in January titled “Serving Christ in the Pentagon.”Most PopularDealsCan’t Wait for Black Friday? In October, despite having no military background, Halverson was appointed chief of staff to the assistant secretary of the Navy for manpower and reserve affairs, another senior Pentagon leadership role that is involved with recruiting all Navy and Marine Corps personnel and oversees policies that impact all military and civilian personnel and their families within the Navy. Prior to joining the Pentagon, Halverson spent 15 years working in sales for Verint, a workforce management software company.Duncan, who describes himself as “executive servant leader” on his LinkedIn, was recently promoted to senior counselor to the secretary of the Navy, an influential position that allows him to help shape decisions that impact the entirety of US Navy operations. Duncan is a former Marine pilot who retired in 2023 to fly commercial American Airlines planes and work part-time at Chick-fil-A. His decision to retire with the rank of lieutenant colonel was borne out of his objection to the military’s Covid-19 vaccine requirements, which in turn garnered him positive attention in right-wing media circles.Last year, Hegseth made Duncan a key point of contact for an initiative titled “Reinstating Service Members Negatively Impacted by the Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination Mandate.”Scheller, a former Marine who reached the rank of lieutenant colonel, was court-martialed in 2021 after pleading guilty to showing contempt and disrespect for senior military officials over the chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan. Higgins, who has also attended the church, was revealed in a recent CNN investigation to have shared scores of racist and homophobic social media posts targeting immigrants and Muslims. Higgins has also played a key role in shaping Hegseth’s Christian nationalist messaging at the Pentagon, CNN reported.Most PopularDealsCan’t Wait for Black Friday? Mikey Weinstein, a former Air Force officer, attorney, and founder of the Military Religious Freedom Foundation, estimates that around half of those adhere to Christian nationalist ideology. For many of those, he thinks that it’s a case of emulating the ideology that they are seeing from their leaders. Weinstein says that the vast majority of the service members that his organization represents are Christians who feel alarmed by and powerless to push back against Christian nationalism that’s taken hold at all ranks, including at the very top.Government officials outside of the Pentagon are also involved with Christ Church DC.Trump administration couple Bethany and Matthew Kozma have attended the church with their children. Bethany Kozma, the director of global affairs at the Department of Health and Human Services—America's top international health diplomat—is known for her positions against abortion and transgender rights. Matthew Kozma is the Department of Homeland Security's undersecretary for intelligence and analysis and oversees all issues related to “counterterrorism, counterproliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and critical infrastructure protection.” Both Bethany and Matthew were contributors to Project 2025.The church has also attracted some personnel from the Justice Department, including David Vandenberg, who was hired to the DOJ’s civil rights division last year and was seated last month as an immigration judge. He worked in New Mexico and Texas as an assistant US attorney from 2021 to 2024. In Texas, Vandenberg’s colleagues complained of alleged volatile behavior.Brantley Mayers, a former fellow at the Claremont Institute, a right-wing think tank, works as counsel to the assistant attorney general for the DOJ’s civil division. Mayers was often a spokesperson for the DOJ, defending the Trump administration’s ICE occupation of Minneapolis earlier this year. He was also referred for discipline in June after a federal judge ruled that the DOJ had engaged in “unsettling” practices in its efforts to get a Rhode Island hospital to comply with a subpoena over transgender care. “That is dirty pool, in my opinion, and the Department of Justice have willfully done that in this case,” the judge said at a May 2026 hearing. Mayers represented the DOJ at a hearing for this case.Most PopularDealsCan’t Wait for Black Friday? (Earlier this year, the head of the DFC was questioned by Congressional Democrats about the agency’s investments and their “potential entanglements” with the Trump family.) In the past, Duggan worked as the chief financial officer for Bentkey Ventures, a subscription-based streaming service that offers “anti-woke” children’s content and is owned by the media company The Daily Wire.Andrew Braun, defense policy adviser for Mike Rounds, a GOP senator from South Dakota and former government relations manager at the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, has also attended church services. Paul Lindstrom, who was briefly an offensive lineman for the University of Idaho Vandals football team and worked as an executive assistant in the Office of the President until recently, has attended, as has Samuel Brown, undersecretary for memorial affairs at the Department of Veterans Affairs.(WIRED reached out to all the government officials mentioned in this story for comment. None of them replied with the exception of a spokesperson for Bethany Kozma, who initially denied that she’d ever attended the church. When told that WIRED was entirely confident that Kozma had attended at least once, the spokesperson said she would call back and never did.)At the church, these officials rub shoulders with members of conservative think tanks, delegates from the CREC network, judicial clerks, venture capitalists, lobbyists, and more.Having like-minded Christians in office is a core part of Wilson’s long-term strategy. “Wilson is explicit concerning his desire to see Christians in office—and only Christians in office—and a church at the foot of the Capitol is the clearest route toward that end,” says Bell.A core part of Project 2025, the blueprint for Trump’s second term in office, was a plan to infuse Christian nationalist ideology into all levels of US government. Shortly after taking office, Trump signed an executive order that established a task force to investigate “anti-Christian bias” in government departments, and Christian nationalists were placed in key roles. Across the government, and beyond the Pentagon, this attitude has been replicated: The former secretary of labor began a monthly prayer service months after the creation of a White House Faith Office.“Doug, in his own words, has always specified a Christian culture comes from the ground up rather than being imposed, and that is crucial here,” said Bell. “Put Christians in office, legislate Christian morality, let that simmer among the populace, and Christian culture eventually emerges.”
